J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges 'A locale isomorphism is defined merely as a continuous map f such that f = h^{op} for some frame homomorphism h, without requiring h to be an isomorphism.' First-choice line 17 is the right-hand side of that biconditional: ':$f = h^{\text{op}}$ for some frame homomorphism', asserted at lines 14-16 as the definition of f being a locale isomorphism. Active assumptions: P3-P4 (L_1, L_2 locales and f a continuous map of Loc), line 2 (Loc is the dual of Frm), lines 4-7 (f is an isomorphism of Loc iff f = h^{op} for some isomorphism h of Frm) and lines 9-12 (isomorphisms of Frm are exactly the frame isomorphisms).

J2_evidence_specified.justification: 'The constant map from the locale of the real line to the one-point locale gives a frame homomorphism h : {0,1} -> O(R) that is not an isomorphism, yet according to line 0017 the map would be called a locale isomorphism, though it is not an isomorphism in Loc.' The two locales, the direction of h, its values and the property that fails are all named.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Model-assisted judgment; I followed the supplied argument and found no gap. The map h : {0,1} -> O(R) with 0 |-> empty set and 1 |-> R is a frame homomorphism: it sends bottom to bottom and top to top, and since its domain is the two-element frame the only finite meet and join to check are 0 ^ 1 = 0 and 0 v 1 = 1, which it preserves. It is not surjective, because O(R) contains open sets other than the empty set and R (for instance (0,1)), so it is not a bijection and hence not a frame isomorphism; by lines 9-12 it is not an isomorphism of Frm, and so by lines 4-7 f = h^{op} is not an isomorphism of Loc. But f does satisfy line 17's condition verbatim ('f = h^{op} for some frame homomorphism'), so line 17's criterion classifies a non-isomorphism as a locale isomorphism; in fact, by P4 every continuous map of Loc is of that form, so line 17 as written makes the notion vacuous and contradicts the theorem P6 it is being used to prove. The supplied evidence therefore refutes the located assertion. scripts/P47_check.py records the homomorphism check on two finite frames as an illustration of the same construction; the supplied witness itself is infinite and was checked by hand as above, and I did not substitute it.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response asserts no consequence beyond the located line: it does not claim that the theorem P6 is false or that the cited lemmas at lines 4 and 9 fail; it only observes that line 17's condition is satisfied by a map that is not an isomorphism in Loc.

notes: The packet never gives the definition of 'locale isomorphism' (line 14 defers to an external definition), so strictly the refutation rests on the reading that a locale isomorphism must at least be invertible - which is what lines 4-12 and the theorem P6 require. A second reader who treats line 17 as a stipulative definition, not an assertion, could record J1 differently. The omission the response points at (the missing word 'isomorphism' in line 17) is the natural diagnosis either way.
